 Lafayette Parish clerk of court says no votes lost in early voting tabulation issue 
 By ANF Digital Team Published : Nov. 6, 2026 at 3:58 PM CST | Updated : 5 hours ago Share Add Us On Google Add as a preferred source on Google LAFAYETTE, La. (Acadiana News First) - Lafayette Parish election officials opened the voting machines used in Tuesday’s election to check them before early voting for the midterm runoffs begins.
 ELECTIONS HQ 
 The Lafayette Parish Board of Election Supervisors met to open the machines on Friday, Nov. 6. The machines are being checked and rechecked ahead of the runoffs.
 The check is standard procedure. It also follows problems with counting early votes on election night, and officials described it as added assurance.
 Lafayette Parish Clerk of Court Louis Perret noted the problems did not affect overall turnout. He explained the cause of the issue.
 “The issue election night with early voting involved a tabulating computer from the Secretary of State’s office,” he said. “No votes were lost. They were combined, tabulated, but we were having trouble printing those results, so consequently, we did not have the early votes until 10:30.”
 Early voting for the midterm runoffs starts on Saturday, Nov. 28.
